Spare blankets, explained for anyone travelling with a pet
They often ask us about it

Spare blankets for pet travel

When a pet is checked in with Aurelia Skyways, spare blankets are kept available for comfort, cleanliness, and practical care. The Companion Animal Travel Desk uses them to help reduce chill in waiting areas and to give handlers a clean layer when a carrier needs to be opened, inspected, or settled again. They are part of routine support, not a special request, and they are handled with the same calm attention as the rest of the pet journey.

If your pet is sensitive to noise, movement, or temperature changes, a blanket can make the carrier feel more stable. It can also help with familiar smells, which may be reassuring for some animals. Our handlers use humane, low-stress methods around pets, and they avoid any rough handling. The blanket is placed or removed with care so the animal stays as settled as possible.

You do not need to pack a bulky item for every trip. If you already have a familiar blanket that your pet likes, you may bring it when travel rules allow. If not, the ground team can use a spare blanket during routine movement between services. Carriers are moved carefully from one point to the next so the animal is not rushed or disturbed.

A blanket should never block airflow, overheat the carrier, or replace proper ventilation. It should sit neatly inside the space and stay clear of locks, doors, and any openings. If the animal seems anxious, the desk can advise on the safest way to use a blanket without adding extra stress. This is especially helpful for smaller pets or for pets that react strongly to a change in surroundings.

If you are travelling with Ruby or another companion animal, keep the carrier tidy and tell the desk about any comfort concerns before drop-off. Simple details about your pet's habits can help the team choose the right approach and keep the process smooth.

For more help, contact the Companion Animal Travel Desk at Aurelia Skyways.
